newsitem.title: USA: House Republicans slam Clinton on Haiti.
newsitem.headline: House Republicans slam Clinton on Haiti.

text.p: Republicans in the House of Representatives accused the Clinton administration on Wednesday of manipulating a murder investigation in Haiti for political reasons.

The charge was in a report by Republican majority staff of the House International Relations Committee on President Bill Clinton's Haiti policy and political assassinations since U.S. troops restored democracy there in 1994.

"Clinton administration officials manipulated a 1995 FBI Haiti murder inquiry to avoid political fallout," the report said in its conclusions. It said FBI agents who went to Haiti to investigate the March 28, 1995, murder of Mireille Durocher Bertin were kept there until October 1995, even though Haitian officials would not cooperate with them.

"FBI agents were kept in Haiti long after the FBI's inquiry had been stonewalled by Haitian authorities with the express purpose of avoiding political fallout for the Clinton administration," the report said.

Representative Lee Hamilton of Indiana, the senior Democrat on the panel, said the report was largely a rehash of recent committee hearings. He said Republicans did not allow Democrats to issue dissenting views before making the report public.

"It was a partisan investigation that brought forth a partisan result," Hamiliton said. "No one can argue that Haiti's transition from dictatorship to democracy is complete, but no one can deny that Haiti has made progress," he said.

The Republican report also blamed the administration for not directly warning Bertin, an opponent of then-President Jean-Bertrand Aristide, that she was an assassination target. U.S. officials instead decided she should be told by the Haitian government.

Clinton has called Haiti one of his foreign policy successes, but the report said the situation there was still unstable, citing the recent deployment of 46 U.S. security agents to protect President Rene Preval, and it said U.S. troops might have to be sent back.

"An administration that invaded Haiti after painting itself into a corner can be counted upon to put American troops at risk to preserve what it touts as a foreign policy success story," the report said.
